editorial:
Imagine being a little kid with a huge heart who just wants his dad back. You meet Bennie, a troublemaker with a golden soul living in the 1930s. While most kids are dreaming of toys and fancy pedal cars, Bennie is dealing with the sadness of the Great Depression. His dad is stuck working in Spain to make ends meet, and Bennie is tired of waiting. When he catches the mayor's spoiled son cheating the system with St. Nicholas' book, Bennie comes up with a wild plan. He intentionally gets himself put on the bad list just so he can be swept up in the saint's bag and hitch a ride to Spain. It is a sweet, old-fashioned story that feels like a warm hug.

You will love how the movie balances the sad parts with plenty of humor and magic. The pacing is steady, and the young actor playing Bennie is totally believable as a scrappy kid. One downside is that some of the special effects feel a bit dated, but that actually adds to the cozy charm. If you are looking for a movie night with the family, you should definitely check this one out.
endingExplained: After a wild journey, Bennie finally manages to find his father in Spain. The magic of St. Nicholas helps guide him, and the bond between father and son is stronger than ever. They eventually make it back home together, proving that love is more important than any toy. Bennie learns that being a good person is what really matters, and the story ends with the whole family reunited and happy.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves magical family adventures and stories about love.
